questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

MUSTER
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Muster"** means to gather together or assemble, especially for inspection or in preparation for battle or an event. (इकट्ठा करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The general mustered his troops for the upcoming battle.
 
 
 
• **"Disperse" **refers to the action of distributing or spreading over a wide area; to go or move in different directions. (छितराना)
 
 
• **Example: **The police ordered the crowd to disperse after the protest.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Muster' **is **'Disperse'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Convene **(आमंत्रित करना): To come together or assemble, usually for a formal meeting.
 
 
• **Example:** The board will convene next week to discuss the new policy.
 
 
 
• **Assemble **(इकट्ठा होना): To gather together in one place for a common purpose.
 
 
• **Example: **The students assembled in the auditorium for the morning assembly.
 
 
 
• **Mobilize** (सक्रिय करना): To prepare and organize troops for active service.
 
 
• **Example:** The government decided to mobilize the army in response to the crisis.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

You cannot lead a healthy life although you stop smoking.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- although you​.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​​

__
 
• A conjunction is a word which is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.
 
• When the** 'although/though' **clause comes after the **main clause,** it can also mean** 'but it is also true that'.**
 
• Unless is used in the context of a precondition and means if this condition is not met.
 
• The clause followed by unless/until is always positive as unless/until are negative conjunctions.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Karan is coming to stay next week **although **I’m not sure what day she is coming.*
 
• *I will not go there **unless **I am free.*
 
 
 
• As per the possible context of the sentence, **one has to quit smoking to lead a healthy life.**
 
• In the given scenario, the conjunction 'until' would serve the intended meaning better than the conjunction 'Although'.

 ​

​Thus the correct sentence is: *You cannot lead a healthy life **until **you stop smoking.*

​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ​

 
• ​​The conjunction 'so...that' can be used instead of 'too...to' as given below:

 
 
• *She is too clumsy to handle glassware carefully.*
 
• *​She is so clumsy that she can't handle glassware carefully.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

I had to hold on to the wall to steady itself or I could have fallen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **to steady itself​****​**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reflexive pronouns are words ending in -self or -selves that are used when the subject and the object of a sentence are the same.
 
• The nine English reflexive pronouns are:
 
 
• myself, yourself, himself, herself, oneself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, and themselves.
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *Jack decided to reward himself with a dinner out.*
 
 
 
• As the **personal **pronoun 'I' has been used in the former part of the sentence, '**myself**' will replace **'itself'** in the **3rd option.​**

 

Correct sentence__-* I had to hold on to the wall to steady **myself **or I could have fallen.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Reflexive pronouns do not work as the main subject but the subject pronoun does.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Myself will conduct today’s meeting. (incorrect)*
 
• *I will conduct today’s meeting. (correct)*
